# Lessons
## Design
- Tune early progression so a playtest of roughly 15 seconds can reach the first purchase or milestone. Use a fast starting income or a cheap first upgrade (a few seconds of income). Slow openings leave the buy loop untested and feel dull. Also keep the second purchase within about 20-30s of idle income, by raising per-item value or lowering the price, so the shop and later upgrades get exercised.
- Give per-event feedback for every economy action: a "+N" popup on collect, plus HUD hints for upgrade cost, affordability or progress. Without it, numbers going up feels weak between purchases.
- Place trigger pads (buy pads, claim gates, etc.) off the spawn path so walking from spawn never fires them accidentally.
- Make moving cubes or other spawned items non-colliding with players (CanCollide = false, or a collision group) and cap their count per area. Otherwise they jitter, stick or knock players around.
- Keep the time to first core-loop activity well inside the playtest window (the probe may last only ~6-15s). Any auto-claim or auto-start fallback should fire within a few seconds (about 3-5s, not 20s), and claim gates should sit near the spawn area, not far outside the plaza. An idle player must still reach the loop quickly. Keep the spec's auto-claim delay and the tested window consistent so the plaza state can still be observed before the claim.
- Budget the whole first-payout path, not just the claim: claim delay + first spawn + conveyor travel (length / speed) should land the first cash-in within about 3-4s of the claim. Use a short, fast conveyor, spawn the first item immediately on claim, and don't leave this borderline.
- Keep tutorial text consistent with the actual flow (e.g. don't say "walk to a gate" if auto-claim happens within seconds). Tutorial steps must be advanced by events that actually occur, or the player is left without guidance. Add a time-based fallback so a step can't stall. Make the steps lead the player to every key feature (buy pad, shop), and check that the guide beam or arrow actually appears (its census count is above 0).
- Feedback should be audible and visible: use verified sound ids from the shared asset table, not weak built-in rbxasset wavs. Add particles or ambient sparkle, and set the bloom threshold low enough that Neon parts glow.
- Shared effect helpers (burst, shake, sound, FOV punch) only matter if gameplay code calls them. Wire each helper to a real event (collect, buy, rebirth, big upgrade) and check that its counter is above 0 after a playtest. Big moments deserve stronger feedback than routine ones: camera shake, a shockwave ring, or a larger popup.

		local resolved = r.Response or r.Reply or r.Result
		if type(resolved) == "string" then
			resName = resolved
		end
	end
	local folder = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild(folderName)
	if not folder then
		local f = Instance.new("Folder")
		f.Name = folderName
		f.Parent = ReplicatedStorage
		folder = f
	end
	featureReq = getOrMakeRemote(folder :: Instance, reqName)
	local resEvent = getOrMakeRemote(folder :: Instance, resName)
	featureRes = resEvent

	resEvent.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player: Player, a: any, b: any)
		local id: any = a
		local data: any = b
		if type(a) == "table" then
			id = a.id or a.feature or a.Id
			data = a
		end
		if type(id) ~= "string" then
			return
		end
		if FeatureCfg == nil then
			return
		end
		local expectTable: any = FeatureCfg.Expect
		local expect: any = nil
		if type(expectTable) == "table" then
			expect = expectTable[id]
		end
		local known = false
		for _, fid in featureOrder() do
			if fid == id then
				known = true
				break
			end
		end
		if not known then
			return
		end
		if evaluateExpect(expect, data) then
			markVerified(player, id)
		end
	end)
end

local function startFeatureVerification(player: Player)
	if featureStarted[player] or FeatureCfg == nil then
		return
	end
	featureStarted[player] = true
	task.spawn(function()
		task.wait(1)
		for _ = 1, 10 do
			if player.Parent ~= Players then
				return
			end
			local pending = 0
			for _, id in featureOrder() do
				if player:GetAttribute("FeatureVerified_" .. id) ~= true then
					pending += 1
					local req = featureReq
					if req then
						req:FireClient(player, id)
					end
				end
			end
			if pending == 0 then
				return
			end
			task.wait(3)
		end
	end)
end

local function buildWorld()
	if built then

	built = true

			if typeof(c) == "CFrame" then

-- Claim detection
-- Resolves the plot currently owned by a player (nil if none).
local function getClaimedPlot(player: Player): any?
	if type(PlotClaimService) == "table" then
		local getter = PlotClaimService.getPlot or PlotClaimService.getPlotFor
		if type(getter) == "function" then
			local ok, result = pcall(getter, player)
			if ok and result ~= nil then
				if type(result) == "number" then
					return plots[result]
				end
				return result
			end
		end
	end
	local idx = player:GetAttribute("PlotIndex") or player:GetAttribute("ClaimedPlot")
	if type(idx) == "number" then
		return plots[idx]
	end
	return nil
end

local function hasClaimedPlot(player: Player): boolean
	if getClaimedPlot(player) ~= nil then
		return true
	end
	return player:GetAttribute("PlotIndex") ~= nil or player:GetAttribute("ClaimedPlot") ~= nil
end

-- Notifies UpgradeService once per claimed plot (covers manual and auto-claim paths).
local notifiedPlot: { [Player]: any } = {}
local function checkClaim(player: Player)
	local plot = getClaimedPlot(player)
	if plot == nil then
		notifiedPlot[player] = nil
		return
	end
	if notifiedPlot[player] == plot then
		return
	end
	notifiedPlot[player] = plot
	callFirst(UpgradeService, { "onPlotClaimed" }, player, plot)
	callFirst(CashInService, { "onPlotClaimed" }, player, plot)
	startFeatureVerification(player)
end

-- Moves an unclaimed player to the plaza center; claimed players are never teleported.
local function spawnAtPlaza(player: Player, character: Model)
	local hrp = character:WaitForChild("HumanoidRootPart", 5)
	if not hrp or not hrp:IsA("BasePart") then
		return
	end
	if hasClaimedPlot(player) then
		return
	end
	local offset = Vector3.new(math.random(-6, 6), 4, math.random(-6, 6))
	character:PivotTo(CFrame.new(plazaCenter + offset))
end

local setupDone: { [Player]: boolean } = {}

local function setupPlayer(player: Player)
	if setupDone[player] then
		return
	end
	setupDone[player] = true

	local ls = player:FindFirstChild("leaderstats")
	if not ls then
		local folder = Instance.new("Folder")
		folder.Name = "leaderstats"
		folder.Parent = player
		ls = folder
	end
	if not (ls :: Instance):FindFirstChild("Cash") then
		local cash = Instance.new("IntValue")
		cash.Name = "Cash"
		cash.Value = 0
		cash.Parent = ls
	end

	-- Load saved data and re-apply it BEFORE the tycoon / claim / tutorial wiring starts
	callFirst(DataService, { "loadPlayer" }, player)
	if player.Parent ~= Players then
		return
	end
	callFirst(DataService, { "applyPlayer" }, player)

	player.CharacterAdded:Connect(function(character)
		spawnAtPlaza(player, character)
	end)
	if player.Character then
		local character = player.Character
		task.spawn(spawnAtPlaza, player, character)
	end

	-- Watch for plot claims
	player:GetAttributeChangedSignal("PlotIndex"):Connect(function()
		checkClaim(player)
	end)
	player:GetAttributeChangedSignal("ClaimedPlot"):Connect(function()
		checkClaim(player)
	end)
	task.spawn(function()
		while player.Parent == Players do
			checkClaim(player)
			task.wait(0.5)
		end
	end)
end

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
	task.spawn(setupPlayer, player)
end)
for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do
	task.spawn(setupPlayer, player)
end

Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
	notifiedPlot[player] = nil

end)
